lol you're going to make me actually say it huh. ok. so i got passed over for this thing. a lead role on a project i basically built. they gave it to someone i trained. and everyone was super nice about it which is the part thats killing me
That sounds like hurt with a sharp kind of frustration — especially because the nice tone is what’s stinging. What part is loudest right now, the being passed over or the ‘super nice about it’ part?

neither really. the loud part is quieter than that. its more like... maybe they were right? like maybe i was never actually the guy. i just felt like the guy. and now everyones too polite to say i was kidding myself

That sounds like a quieter hurt, mixed with something like shame — as if the hard part is what it seemed to say about you. Does that feel closer, or is it more like being unseen and quietly set aside?

yeah. the shame one. ugh i hate that word but yeah. its embarrassing. i told people i was up for it. my partner threw out the idea of like celebrating early. and now i have to walk around the office training the person who got it and acting normal about it
That feels exposed and embarrassing, like the moment is asking you to keep your face on while it still burns. Does it make you want to hide, explain, or just go quiet?

hide. one hundred percent hide. like i keep doing this thing where i make a joke about it before anyone else can. 'oh well guess they saw through me ha' and everyone laughs and i feel like i beat them to it but then i go home and feel like garbage anyway

That makes sense — the joke sounds like a way to take the sting first, before anyone else can. Is it the kind of shame that wants to keep you protected, even while it leaves you feeling rough afterward?
yeah. i guess if im the one laughing then it doesnt count as them rejecting me. it's just me being funny. except it does still count. it counts the whole drive home
